independent_derivation_or_calculation: The misconception that static friction always opposes the linear velocity in rolling is elegantly refuted by analyzing torque and linear equations of motion. A force applied above the center of percussion (h > k^2/R) imparts excessive angular acceleration relative to linear acceleration, meaning the contact point attempts to slip backward. Static friction must therefore point forward (in the direction of CM velocity) to enforce the no-slip constraint. The dimensional and physical mechanics are perfectly accurate.
findings: Friction prevents contact point slip, not CM motion
F applied at h > k^2/R requires forward friction
Friction can be zero if h = k^2/R
